clue.text: But could his degree be in husbandry ?

definitions.text: But could his degree be in husbandry ?

parts.words: But could his degree be in husbandry ?
parts.note: a man with a first university degree is by definition unmarried, so his 'husbandry' (being a husband) is exactly what he lacks

explanation.surface: A question about whether a graduate's degree might be in farming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Husbandry' looks like farming, but here it means the state of being a husband; the graduate with the lowest degree shares a title with a single man.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a holder of a first university degree and an unmarried man, who has no husbandry in the marital sense.

clue.text: Girl unusually' idle gets booted.

parts.note: Ava is a girl's name

indicators.note: unusually means the letters of idle appear in an unusual order

explanation.surface: A girl strangely lazy gets kicked out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'booted' looks like 'kicked out', but it is the old verb boot, to profit, as in 'it boots not'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic verb boot means to profit or be of use, just as avail does.

clue.text: Innocent murderer returns, to America as an historian

parts.note: King Herod ordered the Massacre of the Innocents

indicators.note: returns means the word to is read backwards

parts.note: US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A guiltless killer heads back to the States as a scholar of history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent murderer' reads as a killer who is innocent; it is the murderer of the Innocents, King Herod.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek writer of the fifth century BC called the father of history.

clue.text: With patient application destiny upsets no one

parts.note: one's lot is one's fate or destiny

indicators.note: in a down clue upsets means the words no and one are turned upside down, read from bottom to top

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Patiently applying oneself as fate topples nobody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'patient' looks like an adjective meaning long-suffering, but here it is the sick person to whom the cream is applied.
explanation.definitionFit: A liquid preparation rubbed on the skin, something applied to a sick person.

clue.text: Report made only if this odds-on gamble failed

definitions.text: Report made only if this odds-on gamble failed

parts.words: Report made only if this odds-on gamble failed
parts.note: the report is the bang of a gun: in this game with a revolver it goes off only when the player loses, and the odds favour a click

explanation.surface: A news item filed only when a near-certain bet goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' looks like a written account; it is a gunshot, heard only when the gambler's luck runs out.
explanation.definitionFit: A deadly game of spinning a one-bullet revolver and pulling the trigger on oneself.

clue.text: Cold and hot, complaints of shivering fits

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap
ills are ailments or complaints

explanation.surface: Someone running hot and cold with illnesses that make them shake.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish attacks of shivering are what people call cold shakes or rigors.

clue.text: Stone may be infinitesimal

definitions.meaning: a hard concretion formed in the body, such as a kidney stone
the branch of mathematics called infinitesimal ..., of differentials and integrals

explanation.surface: A remark that a pebble might be tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a medical term for a hard stone in an organ and the mathematics of infinitesimals, from the Latin for pebble.

clue.text: Helper of Burke in his first year?

definitions.text: Helper of Burke in his first year?

parts.words: Helper of Burke in his first year?
parts.note: Burke's accomplice was William Hare, the Edinburgh body-snatcher; a hare in its first year has its own name

explanation.surface: A question about the assistant of a politician such as Edmund Burke in his early days.
explanation.walkthrough: Burke and Hare were murderers in 1820s Edinburgh who sold bodies to anatomists; Burke's 'helper' is a hare, and a young one is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: A young hare under a year old is called by this name.

clue.text: Sent to church in conclusion -or to prison ?

definitions.text: Sent to church in conclusion -or to prison ?

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the church abbreviation goes inside the word for conclusion

parts.note: end means conclusion
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone at the end either goes to church or to jail.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: to be sent to prison is what a judge's ruling does.
explanation.definitionFit: A judge's pronouncing of punishment is what sends a convict to jail.

clue.text: Grand stop in Paris in a humble lodging

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand
arrêt is French for a stop or halt

explanation.surface: A grand halt in Paris, spent in modest digs.
explanation.walkthrough: The French word arrêt (a stop) supplies the bulk; its accent is dropped in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic room under the roof, traditionally the poor artist's cheap lodging.

clue.text: Savoy barman building villa in the sun?

indicators.note: the shuffled villa letters are placed inside the word sun

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: building means constructing something new out of these letters

explanation.surface: A bartender at the Savoy hotel building a villa somewhere sunny.
explanation.walkthrough: The Savoy is not the London hotel but the Savoy operas; Arthur Sullivan wrote their music, measured in bars, so he is a 'barman'.
explanation.definitionFit: The composer of the Gilbert and Sullivan Savoy operas wrote music in bars, making him a writer of bars.

clue.text: Flora very happy with one sort of oil

parts.note: glad means pleased or very happy
I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: sort here is a verb, to rearrange, so the letters of oil are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Flora, delighted with a particular kind of oil.
explanation.definitionFit: These sword-lilies are garden flowers, and flora means plants collectively.

clue.text: Like no thrice-told tale of the Bellman

definitions.text: Like no thrice-told tale of the Bellman

parts.words: Like no thrice-told tale of the Bellman
parts.note: in Lewis Carroll's The Hunting of the Snark the Bellman says 'What I tell you three times is true', so no thrice-told tale of his can be false

explanation.surface: A literary remark about Lewis Carroll's Bellman and his repeated stories.
explanation.walkthrough: The Bellman, leader of the crew in The Hunting of the Snark, holds that anything said three times is so.
explanation.definitionFit: By the Bellman's rule a thrice-told tale is always so, so none of them is false.

clue.text: Canonized princess of 20 returns by these approaches

indicators.note: returns means the canonized princess's title and name are read backwards

parts.note: ST, saint, is the title of one canonized
20 down's Castle Adamant belongs to Princess Ida in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida

explanation.surface: A sainted princess from an operetta comes back along these routes.
explanation.walkthrough: St Ida turned round gives the answer. Princess Ida, the Gilbert and Sullivan opera, is set partly in Castle Adamant, the answer to 20 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Adits are horizontal entrance passages into a mine, ways of approach to the workings.

clue.text: A man of spirit, if 'not discretion

definitions.text: A man of spirit, if 'not discretion

parts.words: A man of spirit, if 'not discretion
parts.note: spirit here means strong drink rather than courage: a man given to it may have spirit but no discretion

explanation.surface: Describing a bold man who lacks good judgment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man of spirit' sounds like a brave fellow; it means one devoted to spirits, the drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A person addicted to strong drink, a lover of spirits.

clue.text: Such things get blown up, making us mute with panic

indicators.note: making means the letters of mute and panic are formed into something new

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something inflated leaves us dumbstruck with fear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making us' introduces the anagram: 'making' signals that mute and panic together are rearranged; 'us' and 'with' only join.
explanation.definitionFit: Air-filled tyres are pneumatic ones, things inflated by blowing air in.

clue.text: Tasty plant, a right one to take your breath away

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
to choke is to stop one's breathing

explanation.surface: A delicious vegetable so good it leaves you breathless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'take your breath away' reads as astonishment but means a literal choke.
explanation.definitionFit: A thistle-like plant whose flower heads are eaten as a vegetable.

clue.text: Opening with the French alarms.

parts.note: a start is an opening or beginning
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: French alarm bells at an opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten someone suddenly is to alarm them.

clue.text: Stopping outdated tax with an empty tin?

parts.note: cess is an archaic word for a tax or levy
an gives the article A

indicators.note: with here means containing, so the tin holds the nothing inside it

parts.note: taken as written
empty means nothing, the letter O

explanation.surface: Ending an old tax with nothing but an empty tin to show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' means containing: the tin holds an O, 'empty' being nothing, making TION after CESS and A.
explanation.definitionFit: A halt or ending, the act of coming to a stop.

clue.text: By which a rose would be as sweet-smelling

definitions.text: By which a rose would be as sweet-smelling

parts.words: By which a rose would be as sweet-smelling
parts.note: Juliet says a rose by any other name would smell as sweet; any other name for something is a word of the same meaning

explanation.surface: A paraphrase of Juliet's line about the rose.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet: 'that which we call a rose by any other name would smell as sweet'.
explanation.definitionFit: A different word with the same meaning, the 'other name' of Juliet's line.

clue.text: Place for a drink 'in the remotest parts of Scotland

indicators.note: the drink sits inside the outer letters of Scotland
the remotest parts of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: tea is a drink

explanation.surface: Looking for somewhere to get a drink in the far corners of Scotland.
explanation.definitionFit: Stead means place, as in 'in his stead'.

clue.text: Gilbert's diamond castle

parts.note: an old word for diamond, or any unbreakable stone, also names the castle in W S Gilbert's Princess Ida

explanation.surface: A gem-studded fortress belonging to someone called Gilbert.
explanation.walkthrough: Castle Adamant is Princess Ida's women's university in Gilbert and Sullivan's Princess Ida.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic name for diamond or any very hard stone, and the name of Princess Ida's castle.

clue.text: Sir Willoughby goes it madly

indicators.note: madly means the letters of goes it are wildly jumbled

explanation.surface: A knight named Willoughby rushes off frantically.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Willoughby Patterne is the self-absorbed hero of George Meredith's novel The Egoist.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Willoughby Patterne is the title character of Meredith's novel about a self-centred man.

clue.text: Jack possibly' found among thieves ?

definitions.meaning: in bridge the jack is one of the top cards called ... cards
the saying '... among thieves' holds that criminals keep faith with each other

explanation.surface: A man called Jack turns up among a gang of crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name; it is the playing card, one of the high cards counted in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a high card in bridge and the integrity proverbially kept by thieves among themselves.

clue.text: He uses reason to discover a rocking-stone about here in France

indicators.note: about means the rocking-stone goes around the French word for here

parts.note: a logan or logan-stone is a balanced rocking stone
ici is French for here

explanation.surface: A thinker reasons his way to finding a rocking stone near some French spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A person skilled in formal reasoning and argument.

clue.text: Note call made by knight

indicators.note: made means the letters of note and call are formed into a new word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A message phoned in by a knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' looks like authorship; 'made' signals the anagram of NOTE CALL.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Lancelot is the Arthurian knight of the Round Table.

clue.text: Does one thus exclude the weather-chart feature ?

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
so means thus, in this way
to bar is to exclude

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about keeping out a certain detail of a forecast map.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does one thus exclude' reads as a question about manners, but it splits into one, thus and exclude.
explanation.definitionFit: A line on a weather map joining points of equal air pressure.

clue.text: Grounds for thinking that collegiate America-is effeminate?

definitions.text: Grounds for thinking that collegiate America-is effeminate?

parts.note: camp means affectedly effeminate
US is short for the United States of America

explanation.surface: A case being made that American college life is effete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grounds for thinking' reads as evidence; it means the land where students think, a university's grounds, which the whole clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: The grounds and buildings of an American college or university.

clue.text: Prayer in the doorway when about to take food

indicators.note: about to take means the doorway goes round and holds the food word

parts.note: an entry is a doorway or entrance
eats is slang for food, and eat is the bare form used here

explanation.surface: Saying grace on the threshold just before eating.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures someone at the threshold just before a meal; 'about to take' is the container signal, the doorway word wrapping round the food word.
explanation.definitionFit: An earnest request or plea, as a prayer is.
